question: What is the Academic Wheel of Privilege?
answer:
The Academic Wheel of Privilege (AWoP) is an equity-based tool designed to help research teams make fairer and more transparent decisions about authorship order. It integrates accessibility, inclusivity, diversity, equity, and social justice to address systemic biases in academic authorship [1].

The AWoP toolkit includes a web app, a manuscript, and supplementary materials such as reflection questions, case studies, illustrated examples, a detailed bibliography, and a syllabus for learning about equity, justice, and accessibility [1]. You can access the AWoP web app [here](https://forrt.org/awop_app/).

The tool is already being recognized and implemented by organizations like the [UK Research Integrity Office (UKRIO)](https://ukrio.org/ukrio-resources/equality-diversity-and-inclusion/academic-wheel-of-privilege/) [1]. For more information, you can contact the team at [awop@forrt.org](mailto:awop@forrt.org) [1].

question: What does FORRT offer on neurodiversity?
answer:
FORRT offers several resources and initiatives related to neurodiversity:

- **Team Neurodiversity**: This team focuses on integrating neurodiversity and open scholarship. They discuss how open scholarship can support the neurodiversity movement and make higher education more inclusive and accessible. The team's goals include promoting acceptance, inclusion, and support for neurodivergent individuals in academia. They have published a position statement on bridging neurodiversity and open scholarship, which can be found [here](https://doi.org/10.1111/josi.70035) [2].

- **Navigating Open Scholarship for Neurodivergent Researchers**: This resource introduces the Neurodiversity group at FORRT and discusses the relevance of neurodiversity to the social sciences. It emphasizes the importance of empowering under-represented and marginalized voices in knowledge production and highlights the need for inclusive and accessible practices in open scholarship [3].

- **FORRT Neurodiversity and Open Scholarship Lesson Bank**: This lesson bank has been developed to promote open scholarship and neurodiversity in academia. It includes various lesson materials and plans that raise awareness of recent debates relating to science and invite students to engage in epistemological discussions and reflect on the core values of open science. You can access the lesson bank [here](https://forrt.org/neurodiversity-lessonbank/) [4].

These resources aim to support neurodivergent individuals in academia and promote a more inclusive and accessible environment for all.

question: What is the JUST-OS chatbot?
answer:
The **JUST-OS** (Judicious User-friendly Support Tool for Open Science) chatbot is an AI-based tool developed by researchers at the University of Groningen and [FORRT](https://forrt.org/) to help researchers navigate Open Science resources more easily. It provides user-friendly, tailored, and efficient guidance to find relevant resources [1][2].

You can try the JUST-OS Chatbot [here](https://forrt.org/just_os_chatbot/). For any issues or suggestions, you can submit feedback by opening an issue on GitHub [here](https://github.com/forrtproject/forrtproject.github.io/issues) [1].

The chatbot uses [OpenScholar](https://huggingface.co/OpenSciLM/Llama-3.1_OpenScholar-8B), an open language model built to synthesise the scientific literature with citations. If you use or write about JUST-OS, please cite OpenScholar [1].

The team behind JUST-OS includes researchers and student assistants from the University of Groningen and Utrecht University, as well as FORRT members [1].

question: Is there a Chinese version of the FORRT glossary?
answer:
Yes, there is a Chinese version of the FORRT glossary. It was made available in May 2026, alongside existing English, German, Arabic, and Turkish versions. You can explore the Chinese glossary [here](https://forrt.org/glossary/chinese/) [1].

The glossary aims to clarify terminologies related to open scholarship, including where terms are used differently or where they are less known in some fields or among students. It also helps newcomers navigate discussions of open scholarship and aids in mentoring and teaching [2].

If you are interested in contributing to the glossary, you can join FORRT’s Slack channel [here](https://join.slack.com/t/forrt/shared_invite/zt-alobr3z7-NOR0mTBfD1vKXn9qlOKqaQ) or contact the project leads [Sam Parsons](mailto:sam.parsons@psy.ox.ac.uk) and [Flávio Azevedo](mailto:flavio.azevedo@uni-jena.de) [2].

Additionally, you can explore how research concepts are defined across sources, including the FORRT Glossary, using the Re-SearchTerms platform. This platform compares definitions in English, German, and Chinese and allows you to contribute definitions, annotate existing ones, and help build a living multilingual dataset. You can join as a contributor [here](https://forrt.org/re-searchterms/) [3].

question: What is a registered report?
answer:
A Registered Report is a type of publication format where the methods and analysis plan of a study are peer-reviewed and accepted for publication before data are collected. This format is particularly valuable for replications as it reduces bias for or against smaller, null, or inconclusive findings, as the acceptance decision no longer depends on the nature of the results. A list of journals offering Registered Reports (not specifically for replications) is [available online](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1D4_k-8C_UENTRtbPzXfhjEyu3BfLxdOsn9j-otrO870/edit#gid=0) [1].

A special review platform for Registered Reports is Peer Community in Registered Reports (PCI-RR; [https://rr.peercommunityin.org](https://rr.peercommunityin.org)) where a community reviews pre-prints. Once accepted by PCI-RR, authors can decide to publish their paper in participating journals (PCI friendly journals) without another editorial round [1].

question: Wie kann ich bei FORRT mitmachen?
answer:
Um bei FORRT mitzumachen, gibt es mehrere Möglichkeiten:

1. **Slack beitreten**: Die meisten Aktivitäten und Diskussionen finden im [FORRT Slack-Channel](https://join.slack.com/t/forrt/shared_invite/zt-alobr3z7-NOR0mTBfD1vKXn9qlOKqaQ) statt. Hier kannst du dich über Projekte informieren, an Diskussionen teilnehmen und dich vernetzen [1].

2. **Projekte unterstützen**: FORRT hat verschiedene laufende Projekte, bei denen du mitmachen kannst. Einige Beispiele sind:
   - [FLoRA - FORRT Library of Reproduction and Replication Attempts](https://forrt.org/replication-hub/flora/): Hier kannst du bei der Erfassung und Analyse von Replikationsversuchen helfen [1].
   - [Best-Practice Guidelines for Psychology](https://forrt.org/best-practices-psychology/): Ein Gemeinschaftsprojekt zur Entwicklung von Best-Practice-Richtlinien für die Psychologie [1].
   - [Re-SearchTerms](https://forrt.org/apps/re-searchterms.html): Eine interaktive App, die Open-Science-Begriffe erklärt und erweitert [1].

3. **Teams beitreten**: Es gibt verschiedene Teams, die sich um spezifische Aufgaben kümmern, wie z.B. Outreach, Website-Management oder Feedback. Du kannst dich direkt über Slack oder per E-Mail bei den Teamleitern melden [1].

question: ¿Qué es FORRT?
answer:
FORRT is a **F**ramework for **O**pen and **R**eproducible **R**esearch **T**raining that aims to advance research transparency, reproducibility, rigor, and ethics through pedagogical reform and meta-scientific research. It provides a pedagogical infrastructure and open educational resources designed to support the teaching and mentoring of open and reproducible science [1][2].

FORRT's goals include:
- Building a pathway towards the incremental adoption of open and reproducible science tenets in higher education.
- Generating conversations about the ethics and social impact of higher education pedagogy that emphasizes openness, epistemic uncertainty, and research credibility.
- Promoting greater recognition of educational resources and advocating for structural change to foster a collaborative environment [1][2][3].

FORRT supports educators through:
- Providing a framework to teach and mentor open and reproducible science.
- Equipping educators with high-quality pedagogical tools.
- Modifying academic incentive structures to recognize excellent teaching and mentoring, fostering social justice, and building a community with existing educational initiatives [1][2].

question: What is Re-SearchTerms?
answer:
Re-SearchTerms is an interactive platform designed for exploring how research terms in open scholarship, metascience, and research practice are defined across different sources [1]. It compares definitions of terms related to research and open scholarship across the FORRT Glossary, Wiktionary, and academic publications — in English, German, and Chinese [1].

The platform enables users to compare definitions, examine relationships between terms and definitions, and analyse patterns in the language used to describe core concepts in research [1]. It was originally developed as part of the doctoral dissertation of Anna Yi Leung, which examined conceptual variability and terminological ambiguity in open scholarship and psychological science [1].

Re-SearchTerms is currently developed in collaboration with the Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training (FORRT) [1]. You can check out the app [here](https://msleungyi.shinyapps.io/Re-SearchTerms_v2/), and read the newly accepted paper in Meta-Psychology [here](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/qsp7x_v3) [2].

For more information, you can visit the [Re-SearchTerms page](https://forrt.org/re-searchterms/) [1].

question: How can I contribute definitions of research terms in German or Chinese?
answer:
To contribute definitions of research terms in German or Chinese, you can join the Re-SearchTerms project. Here's how:

1. **Join as a contributor**: You can submit source-based definitions in German or Chinese, translate definitions from existing sources, or annotate and verify existing entries. All contributors are publicly recognized [1].

2. **Sign up**: To contribute, you need to apply to join the project. You can do this by filling out the application form [here](https://forrt.org/re-searchterms/). If you already have an account, you can log in [here](https://forrt.org/re-searchterms/) [1].

3. **Contribute definitions**: Once you have access, you can contribute definitions by following the guidelines provided in the project. You can also suggest new terms and submit their first source-based definitions [1].

4. **Join the Slack channel**: To stay updated and get support, join the FORRT Slack channel dedicated to Re-SearchTerms. You can join by following this link: [https://join.slack.com/t/forrt/shared_invite/zt-alobr3z7-NOR0mTBfD1vKXn9qlOKqaQ](https://join.slack.com/t/forrt/shared_invite/zt-alobr3z7-NOR0mTBfD1vKXn9qlOKqaQ) [2].

For more detailed instructions and to start contributing, visit the [Re-SearchTerms project page](https://forrt.org/re-searchterms/) [1].
